hints: Picture the Y in your head and count its building blocks. How many separate polypeptide chains make up one antibody, and are they all the same?
Remember that every single chain, whether heavy or light, has one variable tip at the top of the Y. Add up the tips to get the total.
walkthrough:
**Recall the 4-chain structure**

Think of a typical antibody as a Y made from 4 polypeptides stuck together.

There are 2 long heavy chains on the inside and 2 short light chains on the outside.

**Give each chain its variable tip**

Each of those 4 chains has a constant region at the stem end and a variable region at the tip end.

So that is 2 variable regions from the 2 heavy chains plus 2 variable regions from the 2 light chains:
$$2 + 2 = 4$$

**Do not mix up regions with binding sites**

The 4 variable regions pair up to make the 2 arms of the Y.

Each arm uses 1 heavy variable + 1 light variable to form 1 antigen-binding site, so 4 variable regions give 2 identical binding sites.

options.A: 2 is the number of antigen-binding sites, not variable regions. Each site needs two variable regions to work.
options.B: 3 does not fit the symmetrical structure. An antibody always has pairs of chains, so the total must be even.
options.C: Correct. 2 heavy chains plus 2 light chains each contribute 1 variable region, giving 4 in total.
options.D: 6 is too many. You may be thinking of other features, but there is only one variable region per chain, so four chains means four regions.
